shared_turn_1.user_message: Why do mirrors invert images from left to right but not from bottom to top?

Mirrors don’t actually invert left and right. They reverse the direction perpendicular to the mirror: front becomes back.

The “left-right flip” is a perception effect. When you face a mirror, the reflected person faces you. To compare it with yourself, your brain imagines turning that person around to face the same way you do. That imagined rotation swaps their left and right.

If you put the mirror on the floor or ceiling, the same front-back reversal would make it look like top and bottom are swapped.
